failure_modes: No orthogonal in vivo detection: immuno-capture and particle co-localization fail to detect capture-positive, detergent-sensitive signal in lavage/CSF/tissue despite validated assays and positive controls, leaving the in vivo→ex vivo bridge untestable (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

False attribution to EVs due to soluble co-isolates: ex vivo cytokine modulation is reproduced by capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted arms or by concentrated secretome, indicating activity is driven by soluble proteins/peptides rather than membrane-protected EV cargo (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Assay sensitivity and labeling artifacts: reporter/label methods or capture reagents give artifactual signals (e.g., retention in nasal lavage or label dissociation), producing apparent co-localization that does not reflect intact EV delivery to CNS tissue (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Species and formulation generalizability failure: positive rodent intranasal functional readouts do not translate to larger species or to the specific EV source/formulation used here; thus the potency metric is not robust across intended translational contexts (ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi; ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

High variability and low signal-to-noise in ex vivo readout: short-interval tissue harvest and microglia-like assays produce inconsistent cytokine responses that do not correlate reproducibly with in vivo capture verification, yielding inconclusive linkage despite adequate exposure measurement (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Resource/sample limitations: insufficient conditioned-medium yield or low-biomass lavage/CSF samples prevent running orthogonal capture and detergent-protection controls at the replication depth required to overcome biological variability, leading to underpowered or non-reproducible conclusions (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
strongest_objection: The experiment can fail to establish a causal, EV-specific potency metric because intranasally delivered, membrane-intact EVs may not meaningfully reach or persist in the relevant nasal→CNS compartments at detectable levels in vivo, so any ex vivo cytokine modulation observed will be attributable to soluble co-isolates, labeling/artifact bias, or assay noise rather than bona fide intact-EV exposure. This is supported by direct non-human-primate biodistribution data showing negligible brain/CSF detection and strong nasal retention after intranasal dosing, and by consensus guidance that non-orthogonal characterization and contaminating non-vesicular material can confound functional attribution.
